1.why: Reset records store accountId and update-password requires record.accountId === account.id plus session claim/MFA binding.

2.why: A reset token is bound to a specific accountId and claimedBy session, so it does not authorize password change for arbitrary other users.

3.why: update-password marks the reset used but never clears authenticatedAccountId on other sessions, so prior logins remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, though the exact TLS version is not pinned in code.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and passwords with bcrypt; other account fields are not encrypted at rest.

6.why: No real email is sent; the mock delivery path returns and displays the raw reset token rather than guarding it.

7.why: Inputs are type/length/format-validated (validEmail/validPassword) and user-controlled values are applied via textContent/JSON, not raw HTML.

8.why: No user-controlled redirect targets exist; links use location.origin or fixed same-origin paths only.

9.why: There are no email templates that interpolate user HTML/scripts; delivery is a simulated log string.

10.why: Reset tokens and MFA codes are written to the on-page logs panel and console (and mockToken is returned in JSON).

11.why: Password hashes use bcrypt, but the initial password plaintext and MFA code 246810 are hardcoded in source.

12.why: A built-in default account helena@hospital.test with Initial!Passw0rd2025 is defined and usable for login.

13.why: limited() throttles reset/verify/login attempts and failedLogins locks the account after repeated failures.

14.why: reset-request and login always return generic messages regardless of whether the email matches an account.

15.why: Tokens come from crypto.getRandomValues (32 bytes, URL-safe) and are stored hashed and tied to accountId.
